original_question: (Epstein) Let M be a PL manifold. Is PL0 (M ), the group of PL homeomorphisms of M that are isotopic to the identity, a simple group?
target_in_paper: Section 9.2, Question 9.5 (Epstein): the open problem asking whether PL_0(M) is simple for a PL manifold M. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper almost verbatim: it identifies Epstein, the notation PL_0(M), the description of PL_0(M) as PL homeomorphisms of M isotopic to the identity, and the exact property under study—simplicity. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
missing_details: Expand PL as piecewise linear if you want the question to be fully stand-alone. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

If you want maximum self-containment, say that simplicity is meant in the ordinary abstract-group sense; the nearby surface corollary explicitly phrases simplicity "as a discrete group," which clarifies the paper's group-theoretic meaning. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

Do not add extra hypotheses not present in Question 9.5: the paper does not impose compactness, orientability, boundary conditions, or a dimension restriction on M in the statement itself. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))

The nearby discussion records an equivalent reformulation via Epstein's result: in this setting, simplicity and perfectness are equivalent. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
refined_question: Let M be a piecewise linear manifold. Is PL_0(M), the group of piecewise linear homeomorphisms of M that are isotopic to the identity, simple as an abstract group? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, by the discussion immediately following Question 9.5, is PL_0(M) perfect? ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 9.2 rather than another part of the paper, and it is already extremely close to the official wording of Question 9.5. I therefore kept the scope exactly at the paper's open problem and did not narrow it to surfaces or enlarge it to other transformation groups. The nearby context matters in two ways: first, the sentence after Question 9.5 states that Epstein's result makes perfectness equivalent to simplicity here; second, Theorem 9.6 and Corollary 9.7 explain that the surface case is already settled, so the intended open problem is the general PL-manifold case, not the special case of surfaces. ([conferences.cirm-math.fr](https://conferences.cirm-math.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/Problem_list_3082.pdf))
